name: Tryout
why: Borrows any shop card's On Recruit without buying it; reads clean, links every color, and keeps the card for someone else.

name: Gather
why: The shared fuel-plus-recruit-bonus template also printed as Stash and Allowance; nothing red about it and nobody notices.

name: Walk-In
why: Blind top-of-pile recruit (red's allowed exception) with a small gift to rivals; fine, unexciting.

name: Promote
why: Trade up with a rival's cult or the shop; a real target choice, a fair sting since the victim gets a member back.

name: Demote
why: Mirror of Promote that trades down; useful to dump a liability or grab a cheap key piece, but usually the weaker side of the pair.

name: Initiation
why: Round III free recruit up to 8; a big burst a trailing player can grab.

name: Body Snatchers
why: Round Start swap with a same-cost rival member; plays off Foster Parents and Deprogrammers, the victim keeps a member of equal cost.

name: Volunteer
why: Cheap way-in filler that just counts as a member; nothing happens, which is its job.

name: Mentor & Protégés
why: Two members for one recruit; pumps red count and recruit triggers in few words.

name: Proselytizers
why: Steady +1 per recruit; stacks with recruit spaces but nobody else at the table notices.

name: Mob
why: Pays the red-count leader again on top of the contest; rich-get-richer, though rivals can race red members.

name: Recruiter
why: Cost 6 for +1 red per recruit; forgettable and slow to pay back.

name: Patriarch
why: Game End per-2-members count; quiet, rewards the wide cult that is already ahead.

name: Foster Parents
why: Turns Promote, Demote, Body Snatchers, Double Agent and Poach into follower gains; cheap connector with real combos.

name: Deprogrammers
why: Cheap, worth 4, and adds a small sting to red's member taking; solid but low drama.

name: Panel
why: Free Promote or Demote on recruit; strong combo with red, but a new player needs the space rules to know what it does.

name: Loyalists
why: A clean block on red and Anarchist swaps; rivals see the wall, but it switches off a whole kind of answer.

name: Clerk
why: +1 red each round for 5 total cost; the dull +1, forgettable and not worth a pick.

name: Sleep In
why: Big purple for giving up tempo, and it fights the Went Last contest; a clear hold-or-act call.

name: Hold Up
why: Skip the next player, even yourself; a visible sting that can be timed, very purple.

name: Right Away
why: A small double turn; clean, mostly a tempo tool.

name: Last Call
why: Pays for minions held back and claims last; good tension with the contest but two clauses to parse.

name: Crunch Time
why: Three turns in a row: few words, a big change to the snake order.

name: Overtime
why: An extra minion in round III; a plain burst anyone behind can use.

name: Courier
why: Pays on consecutive turns, which purple's spaces make; combos Right Away and Crunch Time.

name: Night Watch
why: Punishes rivals for Sleep In and Last Call, but "per minion on it" is unclear: minions on the token or still to place?

name: Bell Ringer
hardFail: needs tracking a table can't do: requires remembering when the Goes Last token was placed relative to a skip
why: Nobody can read what fires it cold, and the payoff is +1 purple.

name: Night Owls
why: An extra minion after your last one locks the Went Last contest; strong, but "from round II" and timing take a read.

name: Early Birds
why: A clean counter to Hold Up and Bouncers that the table sees; turns off a whole kind of answer.

name: Bouncers
why: Skip two rivals on recruit: a loud moment, timed by the buyer, very purple.

name: Gossip
why: Paid by any skip at the table; links Hold Up, Bouncers and rivals' purple.

name: Timekeeper
why: Game End per-purple-member count; quiet and rewards whoever went deepest.

name: Closer
why: Pays for the same thing the contest counts; a small, readable incentive to fight for last.

name: Hot Streak
why: Once-per-game payoff for chaining turns; strong with Crunch Time but counting turns "just before" takes care.

name: Shift Crew
why: Just followers; nothing to decide or notice, and nothing purple about it.

name: Toast
why: Big silver with a scaled gift to rivals; feeds the silver contest and the gifting theme.

name: Polish
why: Converter; useful glue, no moment.

name: Party Gifts
why: Pay rivals bank silver for followers; a real choice since the gift helps them in the silver contest.

name: Potluck
hardFail: turn flow: each rival chooses a resource to give during the owner's turn
why: Each rival picks a resource on your turn; slow at the table and the gain is small.

name: Sweet Nothings
why: Spend silver to convert while gifting; a real split choice, a bit wordy.

name: Largesse
why: Round III big gift-for-followers that also hands rivals contest silver; clear and dramatic.

name: Godparent
why: Give away a member for followers equal to its cost; a gift to a rival, or a weapon with Old Maid.

name: Hostesses
why: Automatic small gifts each round; it plays itself, with no choice.

name: Caterer
why: Pays when silver is "gifted", a word the table has to define across Toast, Potluck and Party Gifts; passive.

name: Toastmaster
why: Cheap +1 per Silver space; honest filler.

name: Debutantes
why: Once-per-game double silver with a gift attached; a timing call around the contest.

name: Smooth Talkers
why: Silver becomes any color; a strong engine for the silver leader, nobody else feels it.

name: Philanthropist
why: A one-time Party Gifts on recruit; repeats the spaces.

name: Guest of Honor
why: Give away cheap members for +4 on each Silver space; combos with Old Maid and Foster Parents, a bit wordy.

name: Creditor
why: Each round take 2 followers from a rival who gets 3 silver; a sting with a payment, and it can target the leader.

name: Debt Collectors
why: Once-per-game 2 silver from each rival; a contest timing swing.

name: High Society
why: Paid when rivals take Silver spaces; makes the gifts that pull rivals into silver pay you.

name: Envy
hardFail: relies on a rival having more resources than you
why: Pays only when a rival holds more silver than you; rubber-band math on rivals' resources.

name: Harvest
why: Yellow's plain fuel anchor; flexible colors, no moment.

name: Leaders' Tax
why: Reads the board for where rivals sit; a quick, readable count.

name: New Blood
why: Recruit-bonus template with a yellow twist (a new color); fine.

name: Housewarming
why: A free new-color recruit up to 5; widens the cult in one move, clearly yellow.

name: Melting Pot
why: Paid by color variety; plain, rewards whoever is already wide.

name: Makeover
why: Rearrange everything in round III; sets up full sets at the end.

name: Gardeners
why: Fills the colors you lack; a quiet catch-up engine toward sets.

name: Customs Officer
why: +1 yellow when stolen from or meddled; reactive, small, rarely fires.

name: Tourist
why: Followers per color held, every round; strong and clear, nobody at the table feels it.

name: Harmonist
why: Game End per full set; mirrors the contest, rewards the leader.

name: Dyer
why: Tourist's sibling for yellow instead of followers; autopilot.

name: Meddler
why: Changes rivals' resources to break their sets; a real sting, but "one for one" needs explaining.

name: Drifters
why: Counts as the color you need; a cheap way in that feeds Housewarming and Big Tent.

name: Big Tent
why: Rewards exactly one member per color; a real shaping goal at game end.

name: Caravan
why: Resources per color held each round; a bigger, slower Dyer.

name: Jack-of-All-Trades
why: Yellow fills any gap in a full set; a tidy rule bend.

name: Savings
why: Fuel plus an optional shop clear; fine.

name: Out of Style
why: Clears a whole color from the shop; a real denial play that rivals feel.

name: Peek
why: Look at and order the top 4, recruit one; strong, but hidden order the table can't see.

name: Recruit Twice
why: Two recruits in one turn; plain and big.

name: Bury
why: Deny a shop card for a little blue; a small block.

name: Spree
why: Three recruits in round III; a burst anyone can grab.

name: Hawker
hardFail: turn flow: each rival chooses whether to recruit during the owner's turn
why: An auction run in turn order on your turn; interesting, but stalls the table.

name: Patroness
why: Paid every time the shop clears; ties together blue's whole bottom-of-pile theme.

name: Snobs
why: Game End per blue member; a quiet count.

name: Window Shopper
why: Clears two shop cards and pays their colors; a small engine with Patroness.

name: Shopaholics
why: Recruit twice every turn; a big engine, mostly for the leader.

name: Window Dressers
why: Cheap, worth 3, reshuffles the shop on recruit; good value with Patroness.

name: Doormen
why: Pulls a rival's member and hands them a shop one; strong, but the cost rule is a mouthful.

name: Regular
why: +1 blue for buying followers; not a blue idea and forgettable.

name: Trendsetters
why: A shop clear on every recruit; feeds Patroness and Scavenger.

name: Critic
why: Paid when rivals take blue; cheap and readable.

name: Scavenger
hardFail: turn flow: the owner chooses to recruit during a rival's turn
why: Snatch what rivals bury; a fun idea, but it asks for a choice on another player's turn.

name: Help Yourself
why: Scaled steal split as you like; the core magenta move, readable and aimed.

name: Stash
why: The shared fuel-plus-recruit-bonus template again; nothing magenta.

name: Lie Low
why: Steal a little and shut out thieves for the round; a block the table sees.

name: Heist
why: Takes 3 followers from one rival; a direct swing, can aim at the leader.

name: Shake Down
hardFail: turn flow: the rival chooses a member and a payment during the owner's turn
why: The victim picks their own punishment; it feels bad.

name: Poach
why: Take any rival member free in round III; huge and fair to aim at the leader.

name: Cutpurse
why: Small steady steal from the richest; cheap catch-up.

name: Accomplice
why: A cheap one-time steal; honest filler.

name: Grifter
why: Cost 8 for a one-time steal scaled by members; poor value.

name: Second-Story Man
why: A steal just before contests are scored; swings a contest at the last moment, which rivals can see coming.

name: Desperado
why: Bigger steals while trailing; real catch-up.

name: Extortionist
why: A bigger Cutpurse; repeats its sibling.

name: Bodyguards
why: Rivals can't steal from you; a clean wall, but it turns magenta off against you.

name: Double Agent
why: Swap itself for a rival's member; a surprise trade that plays off Foster Parents.

name: Kidnapper
why: Takes members from the widest rival every round; losing members before round III feels robbing.

name: Shoplifter
why: A steal on every recruit; small engine.

name: Fence
why: Paid when robbed; a soft answer to magenta, little to decide.

name: Allowance
why: The shared fuel-plus-recruit-bonus template; nothing white.

name: Splurge
why: Followers for a big buy; a real choice against the white contest.

name: Exchange
why: Resources into followers on a sliding cap; fine, a bit fiddly.

name: Farewell
why: Cast out a member for its cost in followers; a clean white trade that combos Martyrs.

name: Estate Sale
why: Farewell for white instead of followers; a sibling.

name: Cash In
why: All white into followers in round III; the payoff of white's hoard.

name: Recluse
why: Game End per wider rival; catch-up for a small cult.

name: Landlord
why: +2 white each round; autopilot fuel.

name: Heiresses
why: Once-per-game white per member; quiet, rewards the wide.

name: Brokers
why: +1 on White follower actions; a small stacker.

name: Misers
why: Pays for holding white at the end; a hold-or-cash call against Cash In.

name: Raiders
why: Once-per-game follower steal with a payment; a swing aimed at the leader.

name: Cashier
why: A Cash In on recruit; repeats the space.

name: Money Changers
why: Paid whenever anyone buys followers; a table-wide trigger.

name: Martyrs
why: Followers when it leaves; turns Farewell, Promote, Demote, Poach and Kidnapper into gains, so rivals think twice.

name: Old Money
why: Cost 6 for a Game End per white member count; poor value.

name: Hoarder
why: Once-per-game turn everything white, then Cash In; a clear setup play.

name: Build Up
why: Green's plain fuel anchor.

name: Echo
why: Copy the previous action: plays off whatever just happened.

name: Reprise
why: Copy one of your own taken spaces; useful, less lively than Echo.

name: Sample
why: Borrow a rival's On Recruit; a clever link, needs a scan of rivals' cards.

name: Cover
why: Copy an open space; a way around blocks, clean.

name: Greatest Hits
why: Replay every On Recruit you own; the round III payoff for building them.

name: Busker
why: +2 green each round; autopilot.

name: Impersonator
why: Borrows a rival's ability until you change it; the table has to remember which.

name: Impressionist
why: Paid when anyone copies; cheap, passive.

name: Wallflower
why: Doubles copied resources at cost 10; strong only once built around.

name: Fan Club
why: Copies a leader's space on recruit; aims at the leader, a little opaque.

name: Roadie
why: Green per green member each round; a count engine.

name: Stunt Double
why: Copy the action you just took: doubles Spree or Initiation, few words.

name: Tribute Band
why: Once-per-game replay of a rival's whole round at cost 14; big but late and pricey.

name: Doppelganger
why: Becomes a copy of your best member; the table must remember what it copies.

name: Agents
why: Stops rivals copying "your actions", which is unclear (spaces you took?); a block.

name: Encore
why: A once-per-game doubled On Recruit; a timing call.

name: Party Crasher
why: Once-per-game place on a taken space; breaks a block, the table feels it.

name: Alchemists
why: Any resource pays for members; strong glue that blurs colors.

name: Extra Hand
why: Once-per-game extra minion at cost 9; fine, pricey.

name: Line Cutters
why: Go first every round, cheap and worth 3; may be a must-buy.

name: Old Maid
why: A liability you pass around with Godparent, Double Agent and Promote; a hot potato the table watches.

name: Dabblers
why: "Counts as 2 wild members" needs a rules lookup for what wild covers.

name: Anarchist
why: Swap any two members each round; wild power, hard to read the fallout.

name: Spoilsport
why: Cancels a contest you can't win; a block aimed at the leader.

name: Con Men
why: Big one-time steal; plain.

name: Sore Loser
why: Takes 3 followers from the top contest winner when you win none; catch-up.
